Light Up a Life is back at the shop this year, and I'd like to tell you how it works, and who it's for.

Our memory tags will be at the shop from Monday 16 November. We're open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 till 4, so the first chance to come in is Tuesday. You write the name of someone you're remembering and we hang it on the tree in the window. The suggested donation is £3. If you'd rather write at home, there are envelopes on the counter to take with you, and you can bring the tag back when you're ready.

We switch the lights on on Saturday 28 November at 4pm, outside the shop on Magdalen Street. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen is doing her mince pies again. Do get there early for those. Last year they didn't survive the first carol.

Every name on the tree will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You don't have to come to the service for your person's name to be read. Plenty of people prefer not to, and that is perfectly all right.

This will be the seventh year I hang a tag for my husband, Ray, who died at the hospice in November 2019. The first year, I could hardly write his name. My hand wouldn't do it properly and I had to stop twice. Now I write it at the counter with the same pen, before we open, and it has become one of the quieter, gentler moments of my year. I don't tell you this to make anyone sad. I tell you because it does get different, and because the tree helped.

I want to be clear that the tree is for anyone who is grieving. You don't need to have had someone at the hospice. A parent, a friend, a neighbour, a child, a much-loved dog if you like, they all belong on it. Some of the tags last year made me laugh out loud, and I think the people they were written for would have been pleased.

And please know that you can simply come and stand by the tree. You don't have to buy a tag, or a book, or anything at all. Come in out of the cold, look at the names, and stay as long as you like. Nobody will mind, and I'll put the kettle on if it's a slow afternoon.

Thank you to everyone who took part last year. 412 names went on that tree, and it was a joy to see so many of you squeezed onto the pavement in the cold, singing and sniffling and holding on to each other. It reminded me why I do this. We'll keep it lit until Twelfth Night again.

Jean
